types.name: FBuildInfoManifest
types.doc:
A package's BuildInfo.json, applied before the engine exists: crash
attribution and the game's crash settings, the per-product data root, the
build id, the crash reporter path and analytics. Every packaged host reads
it — the player through FGameHostBootstrap, the dedicated server directly —
so a server's crash reports go to the game's DSN too.

members.name: Apply
members.doc:
Looks in the game root, the working directory and the executable dir,
then inside the engine pak. A manifest (or an unwritable game root)
marks the run as packaged. True when it named the product.

members.name: WasApplied
members.doc:
True once a BuildInfo.json was applied this run; the project's own
Config/Engine.ini then no longer speaks for the crash settings.

members.name: ApplyProjectCrashReportClient
members.doc:
An unpackaged run of a game: the project's Config/Engine.ini
[CrashReportClient] section (else the legacy .mproject crashReporter.dsn)
becomes the crash settings every report carries; a project that names
nothing keeps its reports on disk. No-op once a BuildInfo.json was
applied. True when the project configured anything.

types.name: EWindowMode
types.doc:
How the game window presents. Persisted to Display.ini so the choice
survives across sessions on the same machine.
Windowed             — bordered, movable/resizable desktop window.
BorderlessFullscreen — borderless window covering the target monitor at
the desktop resolution (fast alt-tab, no mode set).
ExclusiveFullscreen  — real fullscreen mode set to the chosen resolution
+ refresh rate (SDL sets an SDL_DisplayMode).

types.name: FDisplayMode
types.doc: One selectable fullscreen video mode of a monitor.

types.name: FMonitorInfo
types.doc:
One connected monitor, in the order SDL enumerates them (index 0 = the
display SDL reports first). name is the OS display name; the resolution +
refresh are the current desktop mode.

types.name: FDisplayConfig
types.doc:
The persisted display configuration. Round-trips through Display.ini via
Load/Save. hasBeenSet distinguishes "user has never touched display
settings" (keep the engine/launch defaults) from an explicit choice.

members.name: width
members.doc: 0 = use the monitor's desktop resolution.

members.name: refreshRate
members.doc: 0 = use the monitor's default refresh.

members.name: monitor
members.doc: -1 = primary / current display.

types.name: DisplaySettings
types.doc:
Player-facing display settings: a static facade over Config for persistence,
SDL for enumeration, and Window + Renderer for applying a change at runtime.

members.name: Get
members.doc: Persisted to Display.ini under AppData / the project's Saved dir.

members.name: EnumerateMonitors
members.doc: Needs an initialized SDL video subsystem.

members.name: GetWindowRefreshRate
members.doc:
Refresh rate of the monitor the window is on now, 0 when unknown. Cheap
enough to poll once per frame (SDL caches the current mode).

members.name: Apply
members.signature: static void Apply(Window& window, const FDisplayConfig& cfg, bool applyVSync = true)
members.doc:
Pushes the config onto a live window (mode / monitor / resolution /
refresh) and, when applyVSync is true, drives Renderer::SetVSync with a
deferred swapchain recreate. Persists nothing — call Save() for that.

members.name: ApplyPersisted
members.doc:
Reads the persisted config and applies it. No-op for window/monitor/
resolution when the user has never set anything (hasBeenSet == false), so
launch defaults survive; vsync always follows the config.

members.name: SetVSyncRuntime
members.doc:
Drives Renderer::SetVSync immediately and persists the new value. Safe to
call every frame — SetVSync early-outs when unchanged.

members.name: headless
members.doc: No window, no rendering (dedicated server)

members.name: startHidden
members.doc: Create the window hidden; reveal via

members.name: useConfigWindowOverrides
members.doc:
Fixed-size dialog hosts (crash reporter) set this false so the
window.* values in GlobalConfig cannot override the requested
title/size/vsync.

members.name: ignoreUserConfig
members.doc:
Test hosts set this (and `mbt test` passes --no-user-config to every
row): the per-user Engine.ini is neither read nor written. A path tracer
switched on in the editor's settings once turned sixty rendering rows red,
and a test saving settings would otherwise overwrite the user's own.

members.name: flushCrashUploadsOnInit
members.doc:
Engine::Initialize ships dumps a previous run left behind. Hosts whose
whole purpose is asking the user first (crash reporter) set this false
so the report is still on disk when the UI comes up.

members.name: enableGameRuntime
members.doc:
Physics, audio, networking, SceneManager, ECS world, AudioThread.
Launcher-class apps set this false: they only need window +
Vulkan + overlay + VFS + ProjectManager.

members.name: unfocusedFrameRateHz
members.doc:
Frame rate cap (Hz) when the main window lacks OS input focus, so an
editor or game left in the background doesn't burn power. The Engine
sleeps at the end of each frame to hit it. 0 disables the throttle.

members.name: supplementalShaderArchives
members.doc:
Shader archives mounted under "Shaders" below Shaders.meaf, each found
like it. StandaloneShaders.meaf carries only Arc's UI shaders, so the
crash reporter and the launchers draw when no full archive ships beside
them; test hosts add TestShaders.meaf, which keeps test-only blobs out of
the archive every game ships. Any other <Name>Shaders.meaf beside the
executable (a plugin's) is mounted the same way without being listed.

members.name: archiveDirectories
members.doc:
More folders the named archives (Shaders.meaf, EngineContent.meaf and
the supplemental ones) are looked for in, after the executable's own: a
single-file host extracts the copies linked into it to one of these.

types.name: Engine
types.doc:
Derives from MObject so the GC sees it as a discoverable root. The ctor
roots it; MObject::~MObject auto-unroots via Unregister.

members.name: GetGEngine
members.doc:
Process-wide Engine accessor. Set by Engine::Initialize, cleared by
Engine::Shutdown; nullptr before init and after shutdown.

members.name: WriteRunMetrics
members.doc:
Writes the run record `--metrics=<file>` asks for (Shutdown calls it):
frame-time distribution plus everything that decides whether two
records are comparable — build configuration, commit, RHI and seed.

members.name: kExitDeviceLost
members.doc:
What the host should exit with once the loop ends: kExitDeviceLost after
a GPU device loss, else 0. A lost device used to end in exit 0 with
plausible metrics, which a harness read as a fast successful run.

members.name: LoadFeatureModules
members.doc:
Loads the engine systems that sit above this umbrella (AI, sequencer,
destruction, ...) by name. They depend on the engine, so the engine cannot
link them; every host calls this before plugins load so their components
and scene systems are registered before any scene deserializes. Missing
binaries are skipped: a NoOnline player ships without the online ones.

members.name: InitProgressFn
members.signature: using InitProgressFn = std::function<void(const char* label, float fraction)>
members.doc:
Set before Initialize(). The engine reports coarse startup stages
(label, 0..1 fraction) for a splash status bar. No-op if unset.

members.name: ReportInitProgress
members.signature: void ReportInitProgress(const char* label, float fraction)

members.name: Tick
members.doc:
Per-frame app logic. Runs after the engine-core update (input, world,
events, jobs) and before UI submission.

members.name: Draw
members.doc:
App-level UI submission. Runs between the overlay Begin/EndFrame
callbacks.

members.name: RouteEvent
members.doc: Pre-dispatch, before EventBus subscribers see the event.

members.name: OnShadersReloaded
members.doc:
Fires after a shader hot-reload that changed at least one shader. Runs
at the top of the frame, before Renderer::BeginFrame.

members.name: OnCoreInitialized
members.doc:
Runs inside Initialize once logging, cvars and the object-system
resolvers are up, before config, memory, physics, audio, the window or
the device start. Work that needs only static-init state (the MClass
registry, FMObjectArray) goes here so it still reports when a later
stage fails to come up.

members.name: OnEnterBackground
members.doc:
Mobile app lifecycle (M2.4). EnterBackground runs AFTER the GPU is
idled and before the frame loop pauses — flush saves here, the process
may never run again on iOS. EnterForeground runs before the first
resumed frame. Both also broadcast through FCoreDelegates so game code
can subscribe without subclassing.

members.name: IsInBackground
members.doc:
True while the OS holds the app in background: no frames render, the
loop idles. Never true on desktop.

members.name: IsRenderPaused
members.doc:
The frame-captured render gate Engine::Run used THIS frame: minimized
OR backgrounded. Hosts must gate their scene recording on this, not on
Window::IsMinimized() alone — a background transition skips BeginFrame
without minimizing the window, and recording into the never-begun main
command buffer is a crash.

members.name: GetSubsystem
members.doc:
Auto-instanced MEngineSubsystem singletons, each living as long as the
engine. Initialize() fires lazily on the first GetSubsystem<T>() call —
there is no manual registration.

members.name: ForEachSubsystem
members.doc: Visit every live subsystem in registration order.

members.name: SetAutoSyncCursorLock
members.doc:
In standalone Runtime, Engine::Run mirrors game code's Input.CursorLocked
into Window::SetMouseCapture every frame. In editor PIE, PreviewWindow
owns cursor lock through SDL relative mode and tracks its own ESC sticky,
so this sync would double-engage SDL relative mode and let
Window::NotifyUserClicked — fired on any mouse-down — clear the escape
and immediately re-lock. The editor disables it at startup; default true
keeps standalone builds unchanged.

members.name: RequestShaderReload
members.doc:
The reload is APPLIED at the top of the next frame, before
Renderer::BeginFrame — never while a command buffer records.

members.name: SetShaderHotReloadEnabled
members.doc:
Watches the loose Shaders/ overlay (CWD-relative, the same folder the
native VFS mount serves) and requests a reload when `mbt shaders --watch`
drops fresh blobs there. Roughly 2 scans/s.

members.name: PollShaderWatch
members.doc:
One scan of the overlay on the caller; it requests a reload once a
change has held still for a whole scan. Public so a host that runs no
frame loop (a test case) can drive the watch itself. The frame loop
polls through PollShaderWatchAsync instead.

members.name: OverlayCallback
members.doc: Registered by editor/runtime overlay systems (Arc).

members.name: FrameUpdateCallback
members.doc: Called once per frame for app-level logic, before Tick.

members.name: GetIdleFrameRateHz
members.doc: The idle cap this host was configured with; 0 = never throttles idle.

members.name: SetRenderAhead
members.doc:
Hosts whose frame path owns the publish-time render fence (the overlap
pipeline) disable the loop-top render-thread drain with this.

types.name: Engine::EFrameThrottle
types.doc:
Which cap held the last frame back, for readouts that would otherwise
report a throttled rate as the frame rate the hardware manages.

members.name: IsAvailable
members.doc:
False, with the reason, where Live Coding cannot run: not Windows, a
packaged build with no tree beside it, mbt never published.

members.name: Start
members.doc:
Starts compiling every .cpp changed since the running binaries were
linked. False when a compile is already running or Live Coding is
unavailable (the reason is logged).

members.name: Tick
members.doc: Applies a finished compile. Called once a frame by the engine loop.

members.name: RegisterConsoleCommand
members.doc: `LiveCoding` at the console; Engine::Initialize registers it.

members.name: Shutdown
members.doc:
Waits for a compile still running, so its thread is not torn down
under it at exit.

members.name: RunCompile
members.signature: static int32_t RunCompile(const std::vector<std::string>& extraArgs, const std::string& reportPath, std::string& outOutput)
members.doc:
Synchronous halves, for tests and tools: run `mbt livecoding` with the
extra arguments and write its report to `reportPath`; then apply that
report. RunCompile returns mbt's exit code (-1 when it could not run).

members.name: CompletedCompiles
members.doc:
Compiles that finished and were applied (or refused) this session, so
a UI can tell a new outcome from the one it already showed.

members.name: SourceTreeRoot
members.doc:
The tree the running binaries were built from, found by walking up from
the executable; empty in a packaged build.

types.name: FLiveCoding::FProgress
types.doc:
The running compile as mbt reports it: the file it is on (1-based), the
count, and the files started so far. Total is 0 until mbt names one.

members.name: value
members.doc: all layers

types.name: TagLayerConfig
types.doc:
Tags are arbitrary strings for grouping entities; layers are 32 slots
(0-31) used for physics and rendering filtering.

members.name: BUILTIN_TAG_COUNT
members.doc: Indices 0-6, cannot be removed.

members.name: BUILTIN_LAYER_COUNT
members.doc:
Layer names live in FLayerRegistry (Project module) — the same list the
inspector's layer-mask dropdown and Project Settings > Layers edit.
These mirror its constants so callers keep compiling.

members.name: AddTag
members.doc: Add a custom tag. Returns true if added (false if duplicate or invalid).

members.name: RemoveTag
members.doc: Remove a custom tag. Returns true if removed (false if built-in or not found).

members.name: SetLayerName
members.signature: bool SetLayerName(int index, const std::string& name)
members.doc: Only the non-built-in slots may be renamed.

members.name: CanCollide
members.signature: bool CanCollide(int layerA, int layerB) const

members.name: SetCollision
members.signature: void SetCollision(int layerA, int layerB, bool canCollide)
members.doc: Symmetric — sets both directions.

members.name: ResetCollisionMatrix
members.doc: Back to all layers colliding.

members.name: GetCustomLayers
members.doc: Indices 8-31 with non-empty names.

members.name: SetCustomTags
members.doc: Appends to the built-in set.

members.name: customTitleBar
members.doc: Custom titlebar (implies borderless)

members.name: titleBarHeight
members.doc: Caption height for the custom titlebar hit test

members.name: startHidden
members.doc: Reveal via Show() once init is done, so no

members.name: wantVulkanSurface
members.doc: half-built window flashes behind the splash.

members.name: SetWindowIconFromMemory
members.signature: bool SetWindowIconFromMemory(const void* data, size_t size)
members.doc:
Decode an encoded image (PNG/...) from memory and set it as the window
icon — the VFS path for packaged icons that only exist inside
EngineContent.meaf. Returns false when decoding fails.

members.name: HasWindowIcon
members.doc: True once a SetWindowIcon/SetWindowIconFromMemory call stuck.

members.name: GetHandle
members.doc: Native handle for RHI (HWND on Windows, CAMetalLayer* on macOS)

members.name: GetPixelWidth
members.doc: Framebuffer size — differs from GetWidth on

members.name: GetPixelHeight
members.doc: Retina/high-DPI displays.

members.name: GetPixelDensity
members.doc: Backing scale factor.

members.name: GetCloseReason
members.doc:
Why the window asked the loop to end. A headless test that dies because
its window was closed out from under it (a stray Cmd+Q while the suite
cycles windows, a logout) otherwise reports exactly what a test that
verified nothing reports — a bare exit code with no line in the log.
Three GI rows failed that way on 2026-08-20 and cost a full diagnosis.

members.name: IsInBackground
members.doc:
Mobile app lifecycle (M2.4): the OS moved the app out of / back to the
foreground. Engine::Run gates all GPU work on this the way it gates on
minimize — iOS kills apps that touch the GPU in background. Desktop
SDL never raises these events, so the flag stays false there.

members.name: SetLowMemoryCallback
members.doc:
The OS asked for memory (mobile). Fired from the event pump; the
callback should drop caches, not allocate.

members.name: IsFocused
members.doc:
True when the OS has keyboard/input focus on this window. Drives the
frame-rate throttle: a focused editor runs uncapped, an idle background
window doesn't burn 170 FPS of CPU/GPU. Queries SDL flags every call.

members.name: WaitForEvent
members.doc:
Blocks up to `seconds` or until the OS queues an event for this process,
whichever is first; the event stays queued for the next ProcessMessages.
The idle throttle waits here instead of sleeping, so a key or a mouse
move ends the wait immediately instead of landing in the next 24 Hz
frame. Returns true when an event ended the wait.

members.name: SetAuxFocusCheck
members.doc:
Extra focus sources that count as "the app is focused" for the
unfocused throttle — e.g. torn-off editor panels living in their own
OS windows. IsFocused() ORs this in when set.

members.name: IsHDROutputActive
members.doc:
True when this window's swapchain negotiated an HDR format/colorspace
(r.HDROutput). Forwards Renderer::IsHDROutputActive for editor UI.

members.name: GetMouseDelta
members.signature: void GetMouseDelta(float& dx, float& dy) const

members.name: SetCursorConfined
members.doc:
Confine the cursor to the window WITHOUT taking it into relative mode,
for a game that keeps a visible cursor. Relative mode confines as a side
effect; this is the other half, and it was missing entirely.

members.name: SetEditorRelativeMouseMode
members.doc:
Editor-only SDL relative mouse mode, separate from the game/runtime
SetMouseCapture. Viewport panels use it for FPS-style RMB drag without
manually warping the cursor, which is what caused the visible teleport
when crossing the viewport edge. Engine ignores this path entirely, so
toggling it never fights the InputManager. SDL3 restores the cursor to
its pre-relative-mode position on disable.

members.name: ConsumeEditorMouseDelta
members.doc:
Reads and clears the accumulated relative motion since the last call.
dx/dy are zeroed before returning so each frame's caller gets a
fresh slice — call once per frame from one site.

members.name: IsAnyRelativeMouseMode
members.doc:
True when any relative-mouse path is engaged (runtime SetMouseCapture
OR editor RMB). Used by the editor to neutralise io.MousePos for the
frame so panels under the invisible-but-still-moving virtual cursor
don't fire hover/click events.

members.name: FileDropCallback
members.signature: using FileDropCallback = std::function<void(const std::vector<std::string>&, int, int)>
members.doc: Fires when files are dragged in from the OS file explorer.

members.name: SDLEventCallback
members.doc:
SDL event callback — called for every SDL event before Window handles it.
Used by UI backends that need raw events.

members.name: AddSDLEventCallback
members.doc:
Additional listener, for when more than one subsystem needs SDL events.
Listeners fire in the order they were added.

members.name: CloseRequestCallback
members.doc:
Veto for the OS close request (Alt+F4 / titlebar X). Return true to allow
the window to close, false to ignore the request. If unset, the request
is always accepted. Used by the editor to refuse close while a modal
(e.g. Exporter) is active.

members.name: SetTitleBarLeftInteractiveWidth
members.doc: Left interactive (non-draggable) band of the custom titlebar.

members.name: SetTitleBarRightInteractiveLeftX
members.doc:
Every X >= this value, left of the close/max/min buttons, is a normal
clickable region instead of an SDL drag handle. Caller passes the
leftmost X of the right cluster after laying it out. Default INT_MAX =
no right band, so the whole right side stays draggable except the three
window-control buttons.

members.name: SetTitleBarHeight
members.doc:
Window pixels, not logical ones: the hit test runs in the OS coordinate
space, so a host that draws its caption in logical units has to push the
scaled height in whenever the display scale changes, or the bottom band
of the drawn bar stops dragging the window.

members.name: SetTitleBarButtonsWidth
IsMaximizeButtonHot
members.doc:
The middle of the three caption buttons is the maximize button: over it
Windows 11 offers its snap layouts, and the click there toggles the
window. The client gets no mouse moves while the system owns that
button, so a caption that highlights it on hover asks here.

members.name: Show
members.doc: reveal a startHidden window once init is done

members.name: Hide
members.doc: instant visual close while shutdown proceeds

members.name: GetPosition
members.signature: void GetPosition(int& x, int& y) const
members.doc:
Screen-space placement (editor editor persistence). GetPosition
reports the window's current top-left in global coordinates; the
setters move/resize the OS window (no-ops while unset/minimized).

types.name: Window::ECaptionHit
types.doc:
Where a point in the custom title bar lands. Pulled out of the SDL
callback so it can be asserted without a window: the caption metrics
arrive from the UI in LOGICAL units and the hit test works in window
pixels, and a host that forgets the scale gets a title bar whose drawn
buttons are wider than the band reserved for them — so the click that
should close the window drags it instead.

members.name: RightInteractiveLeftX
members.doc:
"Nothing on the right is interactive", matching the window's own
default. Zero would read as "everything from x=0 is", which makes
the whole caption undraggable — the opposite of no band at all.
